newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GVM says Busang stake not for sale.
newsitem.headline: GVM says Busang stake not for sale.

text.p: Australia's Golden Valley Mines NL said on Monday it was concerned by reports that Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd would advance loans to Indonesia's PT Panutan Duta to buy out the carried interests of other Indonesian partners in the Busang gold discovery.

"The Indonesian partners have ... written to Bre-X expressing their concern at a report in (Thursday's) Jakarta Post that, as part of an agreement entered into between Bre-X and Panutan Duta, Bre-X will advance a loan to Panutan to buy out the carried interests of its two current Indonesian partners," Golden Valley said in a statement.

Golden Valley chief executive Warren Beckwith was not available to comment on latest twists in the Busang ownership disagreement because he was in Toronto, a Golden Valley official said. Other executives were not authorised to talk about Busang.

Golden Valley said in a joint statement with PT Krueng Gasui that under its technical assistance and financing agreement with Krueng Gasui, Golden Valley and its bankers would arrange project financing so that Krueng's interest in Busang would be independently funded.
Krueng Gasui is one of two Indonesian partners in the Muara Atan Contract of Work held by Bre-X subsidiary PT Westralian Atan Minerals, Golden Valley said.
Krueng Gasui and its partner PT Sungai Atan Perdana together hold a 40 percent stake in Busang, Golden Valley said.
Bre-X has reported that Busang contain a minimum of 47 million ounces of gold, making it one of the richest gold discoveries in the world.
The Canadian company is disputing ownership claims by interests of Jusuf Merukh, president director of both Krueng Gasui and Sungai Atan Perdana.
Golden Valley's agreement with the Berukh interests would generate payments to it based on cash flow from Busang.
Bre-X recently entered into an agreement on Busang with interests of Sigit Hardjojudanto, eldest son of the Indonesian president.
Krueng Gasui and Golden Valley said in a joint statement that the introduction of a new partner by Bre-X was a matter between Bre-X and the new partner.
There had been no communication of any kind from either Panutan or Bre-X in relation to any proposed offer, the joint statement said. Panutan is a vehicle of Sigit Harjojudanto.
The interests of Jufus Merukh had advised Bre-X that their interests are not for sale, the statement said.

They supported the introduction of an operator of international standing but arrangements announced by Bre-X were likely to present an obstacle to the introduction of an operator and to expeditious development of the project, it said.
Shares in Golden Valley were up by A$0.003 cents to A$0.057 on the Australian Stock Exchage at 3.30 pm (1630 GMT) on Monday.
